cards.title: Lost between good morning forwards
cards.body: Papa's prescription was sent to the family group three months ago. Now it's buried under festival wishes and cricket scores. Sound familiar?

cards.title: Group chats are for talking, not filing
cards.body: WhatsApp is great for quick sharing. It's bad at finding one specific photo later, especially when five people keep forwarding things.

cards.title: Make a health-only chat
cards.body: One small group, just the people who handle care. No forwards allowed. Prescriptions, reports and readings only.

cards.title: Caption every photo
cards.body: 'Papa, BP medicine changed, March visit.' A caption takes ten seconds and makes the photo searchable later.

cards.title: Star or pin what matters
cards.body: Star the latest prescription so it shows up in starred messages. Pin the current medicine list at the top of the chat.

cards.title: Save a copy outside the chat
cards.body: Save important ones into a phone folder per person. Chats get cleared, phones get changed, and backups fail at the worst time.

cards.title: Find it in five seconds, not fifty
cards.body: A little order goes a long way. AICA is being built to keep prescriptions in one place per person, but these habits work today.

takeaway: Use a health-only chat, caption and star every prescription, and keep a copy outside WhatsApp so it never gets buried.
share: Papa's prescription lost in the family group again? Caption it, star it, save a copy.
